intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that orofaciodigital syndrome XX (OFD20) is caused by biallelic mutation in the RAB34 gene (610917) on chromosome 17q11.2.

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndrome XX (OFD20) is caused by biallelic mutation in the RAB34 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified by exome sequencing bi-allelic missense variants in a novel disease-causing ciliary gene RAB34 in four individuals from three unrelated families. Affected individuals presented a novel form of OFDS (OFDS-RAB34)
checks.explanation: OFD20 is the OMIM name for the OFDS-RAB34 described by the authors.

checks.claim: The RAB34 gene is located on chromosome 17q11.2.
checks.evidence_quote: bi-allelic missense variants in a novel disease-causing ciliary gene RAB34
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature that restates the gene. The abstract does not give it.

paragraphs.text: Orofaciodigital syndrome XX (OFD20) is a ciliopathy. It combines oral-facial-digital features with cardiac, cerebral, skeletal and anorectal defects (Bruel et al., 2023). A prenatally affected fetus had cleft lip and palate, micrognathia, ear anomalies, short extremities, and both preaxial and postaxial polydactyly (Batkovskyte et al., 2024).

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndrome XX (OFD20) is a ciliopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Pathogenic variants in over 20 genes encoding ciliary proteins have been found to cause OFDS through deleterious structural or functional impacts on primary cilia.
checks.explanation: RAB34 is described as a ciliary gene, and the mutant protein impairs cilium assembly.

paragraphs.text: Batkovskyte et al. (2024) reported an affected fetus with multiple malformations. These were posterior neck edema, micrognathia, low-set and small ears, auricular hypoplasia, cleft lip and palate, short extremities, and a combination of preaxial and postaxial polydactyly, which rarely occur together. An unaffected sib was also studied.

paragraphs.text: Bruel et al. (2023) found biallelic RAB34 mutations in affected individuals from 3 unrelated families. Batkovskyte et al. (2024) found that compound heterozygous mutations in an affected fetus were inherited one from each parent. Together these findings show that OFD20 is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.

paragraphs.text: Bruel et al. (2023) used exome sequencing to study 4 individuals with OFD20 from 3 unrelated families. In all of them they identified biallelic missense mutations in the RAB34 gene. The variants clustered near the C terminus of the protein and caused a strong loss of function. Some variant proteins could still be recruited to the mother centriole. Even so, cells expressing mutant RAB34 had a significant defect in cilium assembly.

paragraphs.text: Batkovskyte et al. (2024) used genome sequencing to study a fetus with OFD20. They identified compound heterozygous mutations in the RAB34 gene: a maternally inherited c.254T-C transition causing an ile85-to-thr (I85T) substitution, and a paternally inherited c.691C-T transition causing an arg231-to-ter (R231X) substitution. The unaffected sib carried only the paternal variant. Rab34-null mice had previously been reported to have a ciliopathy phenotype that included cleft palate and polydactyly. The authors noted that these features matched the malformations in their patient, which supported the pathogenicity of the variants.

paragraphs.text: Bruel et al. (2023) noted that RAB34 acts selectively in cell types that use the intracellular ciliogenesis pathway. They concluded that RAB34 is the first small GTPase involved in OFDS, and that impaired intracellular ciliogenesis causes its distinct clinical manifestations.
